01_geometry: Every reconstructed molecule in every frame contributes to the geometry envelopes. The diagram defines the proxy and is schematic. Type labels are inferred chemistry, not verified force-field provenance.
02_spatial_profiles: Center number profiles use fractional periodic positions and 24 bins per axis. Quarter-to-quarter curves show variation; projection uniformity does not prove bulk phase or full-system provenance.
03_collective_stationarity: Collective components are sampled only for display. The finite-cell factor uses all available frames up to each endpoint with means reestimated; early-prefix changes and block differences diagnose finite sampling, not thermal equilibration.
04_smor_cor: Ordinary rank-one SMOR, connected molecular self and centered collective COR use all F-k origins. Full-record reporting lag is at most one tenth of duration. Simulation-step axes cannot be converted to ps without the integration timestep.
05_decomposition: Both self and cross use the same B(0) denominator. Their sum reconstructs centered COR at every lag. Negative cross contributions are retained. The zero-lag self amplitude is 1/G_cell, not one.
06_running_integrals: Trapezoidal integrals depend on the declared upper cutoff. Vertical guides mark saved cutoff estimates. Curves are not certified converged full relaxation times; no tail is extrapolated.
07_block_variation: Nonoverlapping quarters use locally estimated means, with lags <= one tenth of each quarter duration; halves similarly restrict lags. These curves show block variation, not confidence bounds or independent molecular replicates.
08_sensitivity: Centering is a finite-record convention and can alter long-lag behavior. Downsampling tests sensitivity to saved cadence but cannot recover dynamics faster than ten steps. The initial 10% removal is a sensitivity calculation, not an asserted equilibration cutoff.
